title: Ddalgak rules document, schema_version 1
description: Ddalgak's rules file (%APPDATA%\mouv\ddalgak\rules.json) and its export format: profiles, modes and rules (trigger, conditions, ordered steps, priority, pass-through, enabled state, consent). See docs/DDALGAK_RULE_MODEL.md. Triggers use the key names of the hotkey contract v1 (docs/HOTKEY_CONTRACT.md §5) with Ddalgak's extensions (bare modifiers, lock keys). Objects are open: unknown fields are preserved, but an unknown field or step type inside a rule makes that rule inactive, never broader (DDALGAK_RULE_MODEL §9). Cross-references (unique IDs, mode and profile references, self-triggering outputs, duplicate triggers) are checked by the semantic rules of DDALGAK_RULE_MODEL §8, which `cargo xtask schema-check` also runs on the examples.

hotkey_contract.description: Version of the key syntax used by triggers (HOTKEY_CONTRACT §16).

revision.description: Incremented by every write; writers pass the revision they read and fail with `rule_conflict` if it changed (GUI and CLI editing at the same time).

exported.description: Present only in an exported file. Import ignores `settings`, `active_profile` and every `consent`, and adds the profiles with their rules disabled until the user reviews them (DDALGAK_RULE_MODEL §10).

withheld.description: Step 75 (additive): what the export left out on purpose. `env_values`: the values of open_program environment overrides (they may be secrets; the names stay, the values are empty) unless `ddalgak profile export --include-env-values`.

rule_id.description: Stable rule ID, unique in the document. It forms the hotkey action ID `rule.<id>` (HOTKEY_CONTRACT §13.4), so it is one lowercase segment; generated IDs are `r-<uuid>`.

engine_on_start.description: `off` (default): the engine (and its keyboard hook) stays off until the user turns it on. `on`: the user chose to start with the engine on. Never `on` after an unclean exit or an emergency off (DDALGAK_SAFETY §4).

persist.description: Keep the activity list (rule IDs, outcomes, times; never keys or text) in a capped local file. Default false: memory only.

max_runs_per_second.description: Per-rule rate limit; further triggers are dropped with `rate_limited`. Default 20.

mode_indicator.description: Step 72: `auto` (default) names the active mode in the tray only when the active profile has more than one mode; `tray` always; `off` never. `ddalgak status` and the editor's header always show it.

floating_indicator.description: Step 73: the optional floating status indicator, a small badge that never takes focus (drawn by the editor app, Step 74). `off` (default) never; `paused` only while the engine is paused; `always` while the app runs. The tray icon and `ddalgak status` always show the state.

enabled.description: Step 73 (additive): `false` keeps every rule of the profile from running while it is the active profile (`profile_disabled`; each rule keeps its own `enabled`). Absent means enabled. Only the user changes it; nothing re-enables it.

mode.description: A user-defined mode (DDALGAK_RULE_MODEL §7.3). Without `parent` it is exclusive: only its own rules and the rules without `modes` apply. With `parent` (Step 72, additive) it is a layer: keys without a rule of its own fall back to the rules of its parent, the parent's parent, and so on. The default mode has no parent, `one_shot` or `timeout_ms` (it is where every exit ends; `mode_invalid` otherwise), and parents never form a cycle (`mode_cycle`).

color.description: Shown in the mode indicator, always together with the mode's title.

icon.description: Step 72: a short badge shown next to the title in the indicator (a letter, a Hangul syllable, a symbol or an emoji); never instead of the title.

parent.description: Step 72: the mode this one is a layer over.

one_shot.description: Step 72: when the mode is switched to (set, toggle, cycle), it ends after the next key that is not a modifier, and the mode before it returns.

timeout_ms.description: Step 72: when the mode is switched to, it ends after this long without a key press, and the default mode returns.

enabled.description: Step 73 (additive): `false` keeps the rules limited to this mode alone from running and refuses every switch to it (`mode_disabled`); absent means enabled. The default mode is never disabled (`mode_invalid`, ignored there).

trigger_syntax.description: Hotkey contract v1 chords and sequences (one to four chords) without char: keys or leaders, plus the lock keys CapsLock and NumLock as keys, one bare side-specific modifier (RAlt, LCtrl, ...), or one mouse button (MouseMiddle, MouseX1, MouseX2; never the primary or secondary button) with modifiers as a whole trigger (Step 68, ADR 0031; needs the low-level mouse hook). DDALGAK_RULE_MODEL §3.

reserved_free.description: Rejects the scope-independent reserved chords of HOTKEY_CONTRACT §7 in any step. Kept identical to `$defs.reserved_free` of kim-hotkeys-v1 (checked by `cargo xtask schema-check`).

allOf.description: Ctrl+Alt+Delete is the Secure Attention Sequence (reserved by the OS, HOTKEY_CONTRACT §7.1)
chords with the Windows key are reserved by the OS (HOTKEY_CONTRACT §7.1)
Ctrl+Shift+Escape opens Task Manager (reserved by the OS, HOTKEY_CONTRACT §7.1)
Ctrl+Escape opens Start (reserved by the OS, HOTKEY_CONTRACT §7.1)
Alt+Tab task switching is reserved by the OS (HOTKEY_CONTRACT §7.1)
Alt+Escape window cycling is reserved by the OS (HOTKEY_CONTRACT §7.1)
Alt+Shift+PrintScreen toggles High Contrast (reserved by the OS, HOTKEY_CONTRACT §7.1)
Alt+F4 closes the window (reserved by Kim, HOTKEY_CONTRACT §7.2)
Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Escape is the emergency chord (reserved by Kim, HOTKEY_CONTRACT §7.4)
input method mode keys are reserved (HOTKEY_CONTRACT §7.3)

trigger_keys.description: A rule trigger: valid syntax, none of the reserved chords, and no F12 (reserved for debuggers in global scope, HOTKEY_CONTRACT §7.1). Rule triggers are always global.

allOf.description: F12 with any modifiers is reserved in global scope (HOTKEY_CONTRACT §7.1)

output_step_syntax.description: One output chord, or one bare modifier including LWin/RWin. Outputs may use Win chords and IME keys (RAlt acting as HangulMode is a common Korean remap) and, for remaps, a mouse button with modifiers (MouseLeft and MouseRight are the logical primary and secondary buttons; Step 68).

output_sequence_syntax.description: One to eight output steps separated by one space, tapped in order.

output_reserved_free.description: Outputs Ddalgak never produces in any step.

allOf.description: the Secure Attention Sequence cannot and must not be synthesized (DDALGAK_SAFETY §2)
the emergency chord is never produced by a rule (HOTKEY_CONTRACT §7.4)

trigger.description: Keys (`keys`, with `on`, `hold_ms`, `repeat`, `pass_through`) or, since Step 69, a typed abbreviation (`hotstring`). An older reader without `hotstring` keeps such a rule inactive.

on.description: press (default), release (single chord released with no other key in between; a tap of a bare modifier), hold (held for hold_ms).

repeat.description: Auto-repeat fires the rule again (press only). Default false.

pass_through.description: The original key also reaches the application (AutoHotkey's `~`). Default false: the key is consumed when the rule fires. With a remap (no `tap`), the original key and the target are both held.

injected.description: `ignore` (default): only physical input triggers the rule. `accept`: input injected by other programs (an on-screen keyboard, remote-control software) may trigger it too. Ddalgak's own injected input never triggers any rule.

allOf.description: Sequences fire on press only (HOTKEY_CONTRACT §5.4).
hold_ms is only allowed with on: hold.
repeat: true is only allowed with on: press.

hotstring.description: A typed abbreviation as a trigger (Step 69, DDALGAK_RULE_MODEL §3.4): typing `abbreviation` followed by an end character (or, with `immediate`, its last character) erases it and runs the rule. Ddalgak keeps only a bounded buffer of the last characters (the longest abbreviation plus one), never in password fields, during an IME composition or across focus changes, and never stores or logs it.

abbreviation.description: 1–40 characters without spaces or control characters.

case.description: conform (default): any case matches and the replacement follows it (BTW → BY THE WAY, Btw → By the way); insensitive: any case matches, the replacement as written; sensitive: only the exact case matches.

inside_words.description: false (default): only at the start of a word (after a space, punctuation or nothing); true: also inside a word.

immediate.description: false (default): fires on an end character after the abbreviation; true: fires as soon as the abbreviation is complete.

end_chars.description: The end characters; default -()[]{}':;"/\,.?! plus space, tab and Enter. \n stands for Enter and \t for Tab.

omit_end.description: true: the end character is not typed after the replacement.

erase.description: true (default): the abbreviation is erased with Backspace before the replacement; false: it stays and the replacement follows it.

allOf.description: end_chars and omit_end apply only to hotstrings that wait for an end character.

text_template.description: Text with variables (`variables: true`): `{date}`, `{time}`, `{datetime}`, `{year}`, `{month}`, `{day}`, `{hour}`, `{minute}`, `{second}`, at most one `{cursor}` (the insertion point), `{{` and `}}` for braces. Nothing else in braces: no environment or clipboard variables.

app_matcher.description: The focused window's process: by image file name (case-insensitive) or by full path.

conditions.description: All present conditions must hold when the trigger fires (evaluated since Step 77; a condition a version cannot evaluate keeps the rule inactive, never unconditional).

via.description: Where the user granted it: the GUI dialog or an explicit CLI flag (`--allow <permission>`). Agents (MCP) can never grant consent.

fingerprint.description: sha256 of the canonical targets this grant covers (DDALGAK_RULE_MODEL §6.2); a changed target needs new consent.

consent.description: Explicit grants per catalog permission (CATALOG_FORMAT §2.1). Never imported, never granted by an agent.

injecting_step.description: Steps that synthesize keyboard or mouse input.

holds_trigger.description: Steps that last while the trigger is held; they must be the rule's only step.

program_path.description: Absolute path to an .exe, on a drive or under a known folder token. No shell strings, no scripts, no documents.

allOf.description: command interpreters and script hosts are not programs for open_program (DDALGAK_RULE_MODEL §5.5)

relative_to.description: Default virtual_screen (all monitors, may be negative). Positions are clamped to the visible desktop.

tap.description: Dual role: a press and release of the trigger alone within tap_ms sends this instead; another key pressed during the hold, or tap_ms passing, makes the trigger act as `to` (Step 68).

step_block.description: Consume the trigger and do nothing: disables a key or chord (AutoHotkey's `Key::return`).

text.description: Unicode text; \n is Enter and \t is Tab, other control characters are refused.

method.description: unicode (default): one Unicode key event per character, independent of layout and IME. paste: through the clipboard, which is restored afterwards (needs clipboard consent).

variables.description: true: `text` is a template with the date and time variables and the insertion point `{cursor}` (Step 69). Default false: typed literally.

args.description: Separate arguments, each quoted by Ddalgak per Windows rules; never a shell string.

env.description: Explicit environment overrides for this program only (Step 70), on top of the user's environment; names compare case-insensitively and must be unique (checked when the rule is compiled). Part of the launch fingerprint; values are never shown in lists, status or logs.

if_running.description: start_new (default) or activate an existing window of the same program instead.

url.description: http or https only, no user name or password in the URL; opened in the user's default browser.

unit.description: Step 71, additive: how dx/dy count. `pixels` (default): logical pixels scaled by the display scale of the monitor the pointer is on. `grid`: cells of `grid` on that monitor; the pointer lands on cell centres and stays on the grid. Relative moves only.

grid.description: Step 71, additive: a virtual grid over each monitor (with `unit: grid`).

while_held.description: Keep moving in the dx/dy direction while the trigger is held (Step 71): smoothly at `speed` (logical pixels per second; `acceleration` raises it linearly over the first second up to speed × (1 + acceleration), at most 10000) or, additive, stepped: the dx/dy step at once, after `delay_ms` (default 300) again, then every `repeat_ms`, whatever the keyboard's repeat settings.

repeat_ms.description: Step 71, additive: a stepped hold repeats the step this often.

delay_ms.description: Step 71, additive: the wait before the first repeat of a stepped hold (default 300).

allOf.description: `unit: grid` needs `grid`, and `grid` needs `unit: grid`.
Grid moves are steps, never continuous: with `unit: grid`, `while_held` repeats (`repeat_ms`).
A move while held needs a direction.

op.description: click (default), double_click, or hold: the button stays down exactly as long as the trigger.
pause, resume and toggle_pause keep the hook; disable removes it (turn it on again from the tray, the GUI, the CLI or the engine.toggle shortcut, never from a rule).

step_future.description: A step type added by a later version (additive). Valid in the document; the rule is inactive with `step_unsupported` in a version that does not know it.

modes.description: Modes in which the rule is active; omitted: every mode.

priority.description: Higher wins among equally specific candidates (DDALGAK_RULE_MODEL §7). Default 0.

on_error.description: stop (default): a failing step ends the run; continue: later steps still run.

allOf.description: A step that lasts while the trigger is held (remap, mode hold, mouse hold, continuous move) is the rule's only step, on a single chord pressed without repeat; only a remap without `tap` may also pass the original key through (Step 68, ADR 0031).
A hotstring trigger runs steps that end at once: never a step that lasts while the trigger is held, and never a block (Step 69).
A bare modifier trigger (RAlt, LCtrl, ...) either remaps the key or fires on release (a tap alone), so the modifier keeps working in chords.
Recursion guard: a rule that accepts injected input never injects input itself (DDALGAK_RULE_MODEL §7.4).
An enabled rule that injects keyboard or mouse input needs explicit `input-injection` consent.
An enabled rule that opens a program or a website needs explicit `launch-programs` consent for exactly these targets.
An enabled rule that types through the clipboard needs explicit `clipboard` consent.
